source.paraphrase: Inside a declared layer every dependency is statically resolvable; otherwise neither layer nor package rules can see it.

invariants.why: A module name computed at runtime hides the dependency from every layer and package rule.
invariants.fixHint: Import the module with a literal specifier from a layer this one may use; plugins come in as values from the composition root.
invariants.avoid: Building the path in a variable, template literals with substitutions, aliasing require or calling it through .call or module.require, createRequire, eval or new Function, also read off globalThis.

source.paraphrase: Asserting through unknown or any turns the type checker off for that value; a value that does not fit its type is converted or validated instead.

invariants.why: A double assertion silences the compiler where the types disagree. `as unknown as T` is also the documented way to cross a boundary the checker cannot see, so the default contract advises.
invariants.fixHint: Validate the value with a type guard or a parser and build the target type from it, or fix the type where the value comes from.
invariants.avoid: Parentheses around the inner assertion, angle-bracket assertions, going through never or unknown[] instead of unknown, or an intermediate variable typed as unknown.

source.paraphrase: Prefer @ts-expect-error comments to @ts-ignore comments because @ts-expect-error forces an error to be present.

invariants.why: A @ts-ignore comment suppresses the next line without requiring an error to be present. Prefer @ts-expect-error, but an existing @ts-ignore is not itself a defect, so the default contract advises. New suppressions are still denied by core/EVA-SUP-001.
invariants.fixHint: Replace @ts-ignore with @ts-expect-error and provide an issue URL or description, or fix the underlying type error.
invariants.avoid: Do not leave bare @ts-ignore without justification or in a block comment. Use narrowing or type assertions only when sound.
